              'I wouldn't ever do that in my career' - Steve Evans explains Bristol Rovers' lack of draws

              'Yeah, I think we try and win games, don't we?'

              Comments0
              Sport
              Will Murray Bristol Rovers Reporter
              09:00, 02 Oct 2026
              Listen to audio version of this article
              Sponsored by
              0:00 / 3:27
              Instaread

              Since Steve Evans was appointed Bristol Rovers manager in December 2025, the Gas have drawn only three matches. They are also the only team in League Two so far this season to not have a stalemate.

              ‌

              The closest they came to a draw was at York City on opening day, and the 1-0 victory against Rotherham United, which saw the Millers hit the bar in the closing stages. This didn't come to pass, though, and Rovers' record in the league during the current campaign is five wins, three losses.

              ‌

              We have previously asked Evans about the lack of draws produced by the Gas. After 33 games last season, the club only had three stalemates, with the manager saying at the time, "Well, I can tell you. Yeah, it's a stat. When we went to Oldham on Tuesday night, both teams are winning games this season. But the difference is, Oldham had drawn nine. We had drawn, as you said, three.

              ‌
              READ MORE: Bristol Rovers assistant manager Paul Raynor issues heartfelt statement after cancer diagnosis
              READ MORE: Bristol Rovers Chairman confirms one site being explored for new stadium

              "So, I think we've always had the motto as a management team that, if we can draw a game, rather than lose it, or if you can win it, rather than draw it, we don't lose it, because a point's better than nothing.

              "And sometimes supporters imagine teams with players who go home frustrated with a point, but sometimes the point becomes a good point. We need to be trying picking up points in every one of the games we've got left.

              "If you said to me now we're going to pick up a point in every game we've got left, we'll be well safe. So that's just the truth how important wins are as well, but take a point when you're losing is a big one.

              ‌

              It's completely free and you can sign up HERE

              "If we had five or six more draws and I'm sure over the season, I wasn't here early in the season, but there's a couple of games, Chesterfield comes to mind and Bromley comes to mind. Had we taken a point, we'd be much better off."

              Rovers ended the 2025/26 season with five draws - the fewest in the division - and, as already mentioned, have continued the trend of not sharing points with their opponents in the current campaign.

              ‌

              Bristol Live asked Evans at Thursday's pre-Crewe Alexandra press conference whether this is a quirky stat or suggests something deeper about his side. He replied: "Yeah, I think we try and win games, don't we?

              "And, you know, you could see at Gillingham - we lost two late goals - 86 and 90 something. And then people go from a distance, 'Oh they've got well beat.'

              ‌

              "I think anyone who was at the game knows that the first goal changes that game, but then do they realise then I'm playing a centre-half up front and I've got two full-backs playing like wingers because we try and equalise.

              "I would rather try and draw than accept you're going to lose one-nil. I wouldn't ever do that in my career."

              Given Rovers have lost three of their first four away games in the 2026/27 season, a point might not be the worst result at Crewe, when the Gas visit the Mornflake Stadium on Saturday. On the evidence so far, though, we're likely to get one of two results.
